title: Post dialog: show and edit the options that the post script declares

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15. His words: "The "POST" page that popups when you are generating out a program. Should have the "options" from the .cps file visible. Like if a user wanna use flood or mist, the G500 or G55 in its output format. Things that could be defined in the JS code of the CPS as options. To finetune the output even further."

He attached two pictures of the post dialog of a different CAM product as an idea of the layout: a "Settings" tab and an "Operations" tab with a table of the operations of each setup. The pictures are not in this issue. Clean-room rule: do not copy the text, the option names or the layout details of that product. Use our own words and our own post scripts (`assets/posts/*.cps`).

## What to do

1. A post script declares its options in its own code: a key, a label, a type (boolean, integer, number, one of a list), a default, a group and a short description. Define this declaration format for our `.cps` files and document it.
2. The post engine (`camcraft-post`) reads the declared options of the selected post without a run of the program.
3. The post dialog shows these options in a property grid, by group, with the default and a tooltip for each. The labels are plain English.
4. The user changes a value. The posted program uses the changed value. Examples: coolant flood or mist, the work offset word format of the control, sequence numbers on or off.
5. A changed value is stored with the project, for each setup or each program and each post. A change goes through an undoable command. The command has an MCP tool, and the CLI can set an option.
6. The engine validates each value against the declared type and range when the command is created. A value that the script does not declare is refused with a diagnostic.
7. An option never overrides a safety refusal. The verification gate decides before the post, as now.
8. Give the shipped post scripts their first options. Start with the options that the scripts now hold as fixed values.

## Open points for the work

- Where a setting is already a document or setup parameter (program units, the work offset slot, the coolant of a tool), the post option must not be a second source. The option changes only how the post writes the value. Name each such case in the decision file.
- Decide if the dialog also gets an operations list (which operations are in the program). If it is not small, file it as a follow-up issue.

## Done means

- The post dialog lists the options of the selected post script, and a post without options shows an empty state.
- A changed option changes the posted program, and a golden test pins the default output (no change) and one changed output for each option type.
- Undo restores the previous value. The value survives save and open.
- An MCP tool reads the options of a post and sets a value.
- A value of the wrong type or range is refused when the command is created.
- The PR body has before and after screenshots of the dialog.

Safety floor: this work can change posted G-code.
